minutes.headline: Planning Board recommended both the water supply district and accessory dwelling warrant articles, and approved a retail change of use at 1335 Mass Ave.
minutes.summary: The board held three public hearings: the Water Supply Protection District bylaw revisions, a site plan approval for a change of use to retail at 1335 Massachusetts Avenue, and accessory dwelling unit revisions. Both warrant articles were recommended favorably for town meeting, and the retail change of use was approved with a parking condition. The board also met its new land use director, heard a master plan update, revised its minutes practice, and discussed upcoming MBTA Communities work.

public_comment.topic: A Zoom participant reported the town hall front door was locked and people could not get in.
Asked for an update on the master plan; told a final survey and meeting are coming.
Asked for an updated zone map showing Zone One ends at the water's edge (email read into record).
Asked for a notation in the bylaw that Zone One ends at the water's edge.
Asked how the bylaw came about; opposed the special permit requirement for treatment plants as slowing and costing the water district more.
Water commissioner said the special permit step would hurt future treatment plant efforts and urged a vote on merits.
Said the community asked for the special permit as protection against an industrial facility in a residential area on a lake.
Asked about plantings at the retail site; supported the application and disagreed about the economic development committee's role in hindering commercial development.
The property owner explained she wants to avoid repeating site plan review if the tenant changes, and noted the cost of engineered plans.
A board member and the chair discussed ADU owner-occupancy being lifted by the state; a member of the public asked why a hearing was required when the change is state-mandated.

budget_items.topic: Cost of engineered site plans for applicant
budget_items.what_was_said: The owner said engineered plans for site plan review cost a large sum, a burden for changes of use.
The applicant's engineer said paying for peer review of an existing site would be a significant financial impact; the board did not weigh cost heavily.
The RFP work is funded by ARPA money, which must be under agreement soon, driving the committee's schedule.

decisions.decision: New land use director will provide a written director's report with each meeting packet and post it online.
Chair reordered the agenda to take the site plan hearing before the ADU hearing.
Applicant narrowed its request to the retail component only, withdrawing the by-right-uses request.
The land use director will draft the written decision on 1335 Mass Ave for review at the next meeting.
Public hearing deliberations will be included in the main minutes rather than separate minutes, tagged with metadata.
Next meeting set for October 28 and the following for November 25 because of federal holidays.
Board intends to hold public listening sessions on MBTA Communities suggestions from the regional planning commission, to be placed on upcoming agendas.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to favorably recommend the Water Supply Protection District bylaw revisions to town meeting.
The board voted to favorably recommend the accessory dwelling unit warrant article to town meeting.
The board approved a retail-only change of use at 1335 Mass Ave, on condition that a seventh parking space be added if either 1335 or 1331 changes ownership.
The board granted the site plan waivers, including the waiver of consultant peer review under Section 3.7, after the applicant narrowed the request to the retail component.
The board decided that hearing deliberations will go into the main minutes, tagged with metadata, and set its next meetings for October 28 and November 25.

why_it_matters: Both recommended articles go to town meeting, so residents will be asked to vote on the water district bylaw, including its special permit step for treatment plants, and on the accessory dwelling unit rules.
The retail approval at 1335 Mass Ave carries a parking condition tied to a change in ownership, and the peer review waiver means the town did not pay for outside review of that site plan.
watch_next: The land use director's draft written decision on 1335 Mass Ave, due for board review at the next meeting on October 28.
Public listening sessions on MBTA Communities suggestions, which the board intends to place on upcoming agendas.
